analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation and changelog only: changelog.d/flint-native-support.md, changelog.d/scheduler-prefill-fixed-prompt.md, and a new 'Flint memory admission' section in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 516-559). No executable code, keys, attestation, authorization or wire handling changed in the supplied evidence, so no concrete security regression is identified. The memory-admission text says the Flint adapter reuses the existing admission path, introduces no new activation floor or OS-reserve reduction, and states that bounded caches (4 vocabulary entries, 8192 states, 1024-byte keys, 128 JSON depth) do not replace weight/activation/KV admission. It also says state-pool exhaustion fails the constraint rather than falling back to unconstrained generation, which is fail-closed.

Items for integration to check against the actual code, which is not in this batch:
1. The changelog says the request-normalization identity advances to v9 for all models, so providers and coordinators must move together. A mismatch would only lose cache credit. Cache salt is coordinator-authored, so T-041 account isolation is not affected as described. The coordinator side is platform-owned and outside this repo's evidence.
2. Whether the SSD prefix cache (T-041) correctly binds Flint checkpoint precision, the native BF16 KV and the normalization version into its AAD or lookup tags. The changelog says 'Live KV and checkpoint precision must both be native', but the enforcing code was not supplied.
3. The benchmark --prefill-fixed-prompt flag is described as using disabled prefix caching and fresh engines. This is benchmark-only, with no production exposure shown.
T-041 and its SSD cache posture are not changed by the supplied text. The unverified contract is recorded here rather than raised as a finding. The code behind these doc claims needs review in its own batches.
